ai.description: *Rhacophorus tuberculatus* is a 4–5 cm frog with a brown, tuberculate dorsum and pale venter. It features extensive webbing between fingers and toes and lacks a distinct dermal flap on the forearm.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhacophorus tuberculatus* is best distinguished by the prominent, coarse tubercles scattered across its dorsum, which are absent in other similar Indian flying frogs.
ai.habitat: The Warty Flying Frog inhabits evergreen tropical forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in high-canopy vegetation at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Warty Flying Frog is primarily nocturnal and uses its large, fully webbed feet to glide between trees, effectively escaping predators by leaping into the canopy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus tuberculatus* breeds during the monsoon, laying foam nests containing approximately 100–150 eggs, typically attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Warty Flying Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Warty Flying Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation surrounding forest streams.
